== Biography ==
=== Current family assessment, 23 October 2026 ===

The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. Existing father-profile propositions only: [[Glasgow-12|Robert]] 85% → 35%; [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] each 82% → 35%; [[Glasgow-4027|John]] 76% → 30%; [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] 64% → 22%. All five were probable; the first four are now possible and Mary uncertain. [[Glasgow-1024|James]] remains the selected named candidate; no attachment is removed. [[Glasgow-1024|James]]’s own older father stays 18%, and [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]]’s father stays 23%. Mary’s case additionally depends on identifying the 1779 will witness Mary Arter as the emigrant sister. Faris p.13 transmits an unnamed sister styled Mrs Arthur; p.15 identifies Mary Arter with that sister through the tax/probate cluster, rather than an explicit sibling or birth statement. The association remains positive but does not establish her father. Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990), printed pp.8–15; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FN-6 pp.10–11], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FV-S pp.14–15]; FamilySearch film 2055438 Item 5, DGS 007834162, images 1564–1567, visually inspected 23 October 2026. Published genealogy, not newly inspected original wills or letters.</ref>


'''John Glasgow''' lived in Peters Township, Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, in 1779. His birth date and origin are unknown.

John made his will on 14 March 1779. It was proved on 3 September 1779, establishing that he died between those dates.<ref name="JohnWill">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow, dated 14 March 1779 and proved 3 September 1779. The volume is identified as Will Book C, 1777-1779, Pennsylvania State Archives roll 1494, in the [https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/phmc/documents/archives/research-online/documents/Cumberland.pdf Cumberland County records guide]. The will-book entry is also listed in the [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm published index].</ref>

A published abstract names John's wife [[Unknown-764130|'''Ann''']]; daughters [[Glascoe-11|'''Agnes''', possibly Nancy (Glascoe) Wright]] and [[Glasgow-4028|a daughter rendered “Lates,” possibly Lettice]]; son [[Glasgow-4029|'''Joseph''']]; and an unborn child. The witnesses were [[Glasgow-1543|'''Joseph Glasgow''']], James Neely and Mary Arter.<ref name="JohnWill" /> The adult witness Joseph is a candidate for John's brother and is distinct from John's son Joseph. The original will image should be inspected before treating the uncertain daughter's name or the proposed Nancy/Agnes identification as final.

== Research Notes ==
=== Peters Township family review,20 October 2026 ===

'''Earlier research argument, superseded for fatherhood on 23 October 2026:'''
Peters Township family: two strongly supported child links at 98%, Nancy/Agnes only possible at 37%, and James of Moneymore now probable father at 76%.

Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. [[Glasgow-4028|Lates Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph Glasgow]] are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

'''Earlier research argument, superseded for fatherhood on 23 October 2026:'''
Assess James of Moneymore, [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow II]], as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The older James-1025 father of James-1024 remains 18%; no Scottish migration, Mary Harkness maternity, new mother, identity merge or live edit follows. Exact percentages express individual subjective judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied independent probabilities.<ref>[https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdclccn/57/05/15/50/57051550/57051550.pdf#page=88 Virginia Shannon Fendrick, American Revolutionary Soldiers of Franklin County, Pennsylvania (1944), printed p.88, PDF p.88, Joseph Glassgo entry; page visually checked 20 October 2026]; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm Cumberland will-book index: John Glasgow, C161; checked 20 October 2026]; [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ Joyce Wilson, Our Ancestors of Adams County,29March2024; secondary account checked 20 October 2026]. The 1944 abstract, not the original will, was inspected.</ref>

=== Birth estimate ===

The profile uses “before 1758” only as an estimate. John was an adult testator with children by March 1779, but no located record states his age or birthplace.

=== Possible brothers ===

David Faris's catalogue summary says that [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]] emigrated to Pennsylvania in 1769 with three brothers and one sister.<ref name="Faris">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (1990), [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 WorldCat catalogue summary].</ref> [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]], [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] and Robert are independently identified as brothers.

A later Adams County family-history account identifies this John as their brother and says that Joseph, Robert and Arthur moved to Virginia after John's death.<ref name="AdamsCounty">Joyce Wilson, “Our Ancestors of Adams County,” ''People's Defender'', 29 March 2024, [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ online article]. This is a secondary family-history account.</ref> Joseph Glasgow's appearance as a witness to John's will supplies a contemporary association, and the proposed relationship fits Faris's count of four brothers.

Neither the witness relationship nor the later family account is primary proof that John was their brother. He has been attached to the proposed sibling group and parents with uncertain relationship status pending stronger evidence.

=== Records sought ===

* The original Cumberland County Will Book C, page 161 entry and any surviving probate packet.
* Guardianship records for John's minor or unborn children.
* Estate accounts, sale records and bonds identifying relatives.
* Evidence connecting the witness Joseph Glasgow to [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph Glasgow of Wythe County]].


=== Neely associate network ===

James Neely was one of the witnesses to John's 1779 will.<ref name="NeelyWillNetwork">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow, dated 14 March 1779 and proved 3 September 1779; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm will-book index].</ref>

A generation later, [[Glasgow-563|William Glasgow]], son of John's proposed brother [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]], married [[Montgomery-6593|Rhoda '''Neely''' Montgomery]]. The couple also used the name for a daughter, Rhoda Neely Glasgow. A published Adams County family account identifies William and Rhoda and separately identifies John as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph.<ref name="AdamsCountyNeely">Joyce Wilson, "Our Ancestors of Adams County," ''People's Defender'', 29 March 2024, [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ online article]. This is a secondary family-history account.</ref>

The recurring Neely name is consistent with a continuing family or associate network and adds circumstantial support to the proposed brother relationship. No record yet identifies James Neely as Rhoda's namesake or relative, and the origin of Rhoda's middle name remains unexplained. This evidence is therefore supportive rather than proof.

=== Possible John Glascow, Chester County land and committee ===
John Glascow is an adjoining landholder in a West-Nottingham Township, Chester County execution-sale notice for 22½ acres, late Michael Dintz’s estate, bounded by Abraham Bunting, John Glascow and others.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401494/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1773-04-28, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401765/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1773-05-05, p.5].</ref>

John Glascow is appointed to provide for distressed families of Associators in actual service by the Chester County Committee of Inspection and Observation, in a resolution dated 13 August 1776.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398635/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1776-08-28, p.3].</ref>

The adjoining-owner and committee appointments may concern one man but do not name his parents or wife. They require an active adult in 1773 and 1776; the John who died in May 1769 cannot be that living participant.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4027]]. possible, geographically relevant but chronology uncertain. Potentially alive and adult in August 1776; a Pennsylvania location and compatible time range make him worth comparing. The death qualifier permits death either before or after the roster date, so it is not a concrete exclusion. Public tree lists parents James Glasgow II (Glasgow-1024) and Mary Harkness, but this tree relationship is unmarked/uncertain and supplies no link to the roster.
